prompt.context_jp: 意地だけ___、彼をミシンの前に座らせ続けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 意地だけ___、彼をミシンの前に座らせ続けていた。

feedback.correct_en: 'だけが' exhaustively identifies stubbornness as the sole thing keeping him at the machine — exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'stubbornness' into a topic and lose the 'only this and nothing else' nuance. を doesn't fit this intransitive causative subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 意地だけが支えだった。

prompt.context_jp: 夜はすっかり更け、家の中にはミシンの音だけ___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家の中にはミシンの音だけ___響いていた。

feedback.correct_en: The sewing-machine sound is newly introduced as the only thing audible — exhaustive-listing が after だけ.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like topicalizing 'just the sound', which is odd for a scene-setting description. に doesn't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 風の音だけが聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: Only the wind could be heard.

contrast_examples.jp: ミシンの音は うるさい。

prompt.context_jp: 何度やり直しても、布___思うようにまっすぐ進んでくれない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 何度やり直しても、布___思うようにまっすぐ進んでくれない。

feedback.correct_en: は marks 布 as the topic/contrast — 'as for the fabric, it won't go straight (contrary to his wishes)'. This contrastive は captures his frustration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 布 as new information, but the fabric is already the thing he's been struggling with. を can't appear with 進む here.

contrast_examples.jp: 布はまっすぐ進まない。
contrast_examples.en: The fabric (as for it) won't go straight.

prompt.context_jp: 家の門の前に、荷物を抱えた女性___ひとり立っているのが見えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 荷物を抱えた女性___ひとり立っているのが見えた。

feedback.correct_en: The woman is being introduced for the first time into the scene — classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は presupposes the woman is already a known topic, but Kazuyuki is just noticing her. に doesn't mark the subject of 立っている here.

contrast_examples.jp: 知らない人が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: An unknown person was standing (new info).

contrast_examples.jp: その人はまだ立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: That person (already known) was still standing.

prompt.context_jp: だってさ やましいこと___なけりゃ 消す必要なんかないんだからさ
prompt.prompt_jp: やましいこと___なけりゃ 消す必要なんかない。

feedback.correct_en: In the conditional 'if there isn't X', the existence of やましいこと is being asserted/denied — subject of ない, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would contrast やましいこと with something else, which doesn't fit this casual 'if there's nothing shady' logic. を can't mark the subject of ない.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間がなければ無理だ。
contrast_examples.en: If there's no time, it's impossible.

contrast_examples.jp: お金はないけど、時間はある。
contrast_examples.en: I don't have money but I have time (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: まず姿勢___悪いんですよ
prompt.prompt_jp: まず姿勢___悪いんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: Yusuke is pointing out what's wrong — 姿勢 is new focused information identifying the problem. Exhaustive/identifying が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 姿勢 a known topic, weakening the 'THIS is what's wrong' diagnosis Yusuke is delivering.

prompt.context_jp: お前___働いて俺___家にいることさ
prompt.prompt_jp: お前___働いて俺___家にいること。

feedback.correct_en: Both clauses describe who does what in an identifying/contrastive-focus frame; が emphasizes 'YOU work and I stay home' as the surprising reversal.
feedback.incorrect_en: は/は would flatten it into a neutral topical statement and lose the 'these specific people in these specific roles' identification central to his embarrassment.

contrast_examples.jp: 妻が働いて夫が家にいる。
contrast_examples.en: The wife works and the husband stays home (identifying who does what).

contrast_examples.jp: 私は会社員で、妻は主婦です。
contrast_examples.en: I'm an office worker; my wife is a housewife (neutral topics).

prompt.context_jp: 美紀___どこ行ってるの？
prompt.prompt_jp: 美紀___どこ行ってるの？

feedback.correct_en: Miki is the known topic of the question — 'as for Miki, where has she gone?'. Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 美紀がどこ行ってるの would sound like identifying which person went (e.g., out of several), which doesn't match the mother casually asking after her daughter.

prompt.context_jp: いや 潰れたの___子会社なんですが
prompt.prompt_jp: 潰れたの___子会社なんです。

feedback.correct_en: 'The thing that went bankrupt' is now the established topic from the previous turn; は marks it and contrasts 子会社 with the parent company she assumed.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 潰れたの as brand-new information, but she just asked about it. Clefts like 〜のは〜だ almost always use は.

contrast_examples.en: The one who failed is me (cleft, は).
I'm the one who failed (identifying が).

prompt.context_jp: どうして美紀___働いてるの？
prompt.prompt_jp: どうして美紀___働いてるの？

feedback.correct_en: The mother is questioning the whole situation and focusing on Miki as the one working (not the husband) — identifying/contrastive-focus が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 美紀はなぜ働いてるの would sound more like a neutral inquiry about Miki in general; here the surprise is 'why is MIKI the one working (and not Kazuyuki)?'

contrast_examples.en: Why are YOU the one coming?

prompt.context_jp: ほっとしたのも束の間、電話___鳴り出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 電話___鳴り出した。

feedback.correct_en: The phone ringing is a sudden new event breaking into the scene — classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 電話は鳴り出した would presuppose the phone as a known topic, which doesn't fit this surprise moment.

prompt.context_jp: みんな 「スパーブ」の創刊号___できました
prompt.prompt_jp: 「スパーブ」の創刊号___できました。

feedback.correct_en: The editor-in-chief is announcing new information — the first issue has arrived. New-info が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a background topic ('as for the first issue...'), losing the announcing-a-fresh-event feel.

prompt.context_jp: 彼はプライド___押し殺して、隣のカリスマ主夫の家の呼び鈴を鳴らした。
prompt.prompt_jp: プライド___押し殺して

feedback.correct_en: プライドを押し殺す ('swallow one's pride') is a transitive collocation; プライド is the direct object of 押し殺す.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as subject, but it's what he's suppressing. に doesn't fit this transitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: 夜の山村家のリビング___、和之はミシンの前に背中を丸めて座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: リビング___、和之はミシンの前に座っていた。

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action (sitting and sewing) takes place.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark pure existence/location but 座る here is an ongoing action in a space. を doesn't mark location.

contrast_examples.en: Work in the living room (action location).

prompt.context_jp: 理絵を幼稚園___送り出したあと、家の中は急に静かになった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 理絵を幼稚園___送り出した。

feedback.correct_en: に marks the destination of the sending/departure.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark where the action occurs, but 幼稚園 here is the endpoint. が doesn't work syntactically.

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ 隣のやつもそうですよ」「あの人___そうなの？」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの人___そうなの？

feedback.correct_en: Kazuyuki just said 'the guy next door too', and Mitsue echoes the 'also' with も — 'that person too?'
feedback.incorrect_en: が or は would lose the 'also/too' meaning that's central to her surprise that the neighbor is ALSO a househusband.

prompt.context_jp: おばあちゃんの___一番おいしい
prompt.prompt_jp: おばあちゃんの___一番おいしい。

feedback.correct_en: 'Grandma's is THE most delicious' — picking out one from a set (grandma vs. mom vs. dad). Exhaustive/identifying が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mean 'as for grandma's, it's the tastiest', losing the ranking/selection nuance that suits Rie's comparison.

contrast_examples.en: THIS is what I like most (selecting).

prompt.context_jp: 人を傷つけないように 気___使うってことは― まだ できないから
prompt.prompt_jp: 気___使うってこと

feedback.correct_en: 気を使う ('be considerate / show concern') is a fixed collocation; 気 is the direct object of 使う.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気がする means 'feel like', different meaning. 気は使う would mark 気 as a contrastive topic, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 気を使ってくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: 今は一本の糸に___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今は一本の糸に___。

feedback.correct_en: 振り回される = 'be jerked around / tossed about' — exactly the irony of a man who once directed dozens of staff now being defeated by one thread.
feedback.incorrect_en: 動かしている is active 'moving', the opposite nuance. 押している doesn't match this idiomatic usage.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供に振り回される毎日。
contrast_examples.en: Days of being jerked around by the kids.

prompt.context_jp: 美紀に押しつけられた役目が、___に重くつかえている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___に重くつかえている。

feedback.correct_en: 喉の奥につかえる is the idiomatic way to describe words/duties stuck and hard to come out — exactly his inability to confess.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頭の上/足の裏 don't form this idiom. The feeling of being unable to speak lives in the throat in Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: The words get stuck in my throat.
Feel a lump in one's chest.

prompt.context_jp: 大の男が主夫なんて ___が悪いじゃないの
prompt.prompt_jp: 大の男が主夫なんて ___が悪いじゃないの。

feedback.correct_en: 世間体が悪い = 'looks bad to others / embarrassing socially' — fits Mitsue's old-fashioned concern about appearances.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気持ちが悪い means 'feels gross/nauseous' — wrong meaning. 都合が悪い means 'inconvenient', also doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: Worry about how it looks to society.

prompt.context_jp: いい年して親の___かじるなんて やだもんねえ
prompt.prompt_jp: いい年して親の___かじるなんて

feedback.correct_en: 親のすねをかじる ('gnaw on one's parent's shin') is the fixed idiom for 'live off / sponge off one's parents'.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other body parts don't form this idiom. The image is specifically of the shin.

contrast_examples.jp: いつまで親のすねをかじってるの？
contrast_examples.en: How long will you keep leeching off your parents?

prompt.context_jp: 義母が来てまだ半日も経たないというのに、ひどく___。
prompt.prompt_jp: ひどく___。

feedback.correct_en: 疲れ果てる = 'be utterly exhausted'; fits the context of the half-day of mother-in-law stress.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options contradict his clearly worn-out state after dealing with Mitsue.

contrast_examples.jp: 一日中働いて疲れ果てた。
contrast_examples.en: Worked all day and was exhausted.

prompt.context_jp: そしたらさ ホームページの 閲覧履歴 全部___
prompt.prompt_jp: 閲覧履歴 全部___

feedback.correct_en: Saeko's suspicion is that the browsing history is being erased — 消去される.
feedback.incorrect_en: 保存 (saved) or 印刷 (printed) wouldn't give her any reason to suspect her husband of hiding something.

prompt.context_jp: 自分ひとりの力ではどうにもならないことは昨夜で___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 昨夜で___。

feedback.correct_en: 身に染みる = 'feel deeply / learn painfully from experience' — fits how last night's failure drove the lesson home.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目に入る means 'come into view'; 手に取る means 'pick up'. Neither matches the deep realization nuance.

contrast_examples.en: The cold goes right through me.

contrast_examples.jp: 親のありがたみが身に染みる。
contrast_examples.en: I deeply feel my parents' kindness.

prompt.context_jp: 居場所をなくした和之は、___に外へ出た。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___に外へ出た。

feedback.correct_en: 手持ちぶさた describes having nothing to do / feeling idle — exactly Kazuyuki's state after being displaced from his own housework.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other four-character expressions are unrelated in meaning.

contrast_examples.en: Not knowing what to do with oneself.

prompt.context_jp: 美紀『私 代わろうか？』 和之『____』(Kazuyuki wants to decline his wife's offer, still stubborn)
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply sounds most natural for Kazuyuki here?

choices.text: いや もう終わるから
いいえ、ただいま終了いたします
結構です、まもなく完了予定でございます

feedback.correct_en: Casual, clipped 'いや もう終わるから' matches a husband brushing off help at home — register and stubbornness both fit.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are extremely formal business/keigo registers that would be absurd between spouses in pajamas at night.

contrast_examples.jp: いや、もうすぐ終わるから。
まもなく完了いたします。
contrast_examples.en: It will be completed shortly (to boss/client).

prompt.context_jp: Mother-in-law speaking to son-in-law Kazuyuki as he makes her tea
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural coming from Mitsue?

choices.text: 悪いわね 旦那さんにそんなことさせちゃって
すまないな お前にそんなことやらせちゃって
誠に恐縮でございます、ご主人様

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses a warm, slightly feminine register (わね、〜させちゃって) typical of an older woman speaking to her son-in-law. It matches how Mitsue actually speaks.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is gruff masculine speech, wrong for Mitsue. C is exaggerated keigo inappropriate for family.

contrast_examples.jp: 悪いわねえ、気を使わせちゃって。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry to make you go to the trouble.
My deepest apologies (too formal for family).

prompt.context_jp: Yusuke taking a work call at home (phone business register)
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing sounds most natural for a polite business phone call?

choices.text: 結論が出次第 ご連絡します はい はい どうも失礼します
結論出たら連絡するね じゃあね バイバイ
結論出るからさ 待ってて 切るよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜次第ご連絡します and 失礼します are standard polite business phone closings — exactly what Yusuke uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C are casual friend-register phrases, totally out of place in a work call.

contrast_examples.jp: 分かり次第ご連絡いたします。
contrast_examples.en: I'll contact you as soon as I know.

contrast_examples.jp: 分かったら連絡するね。
contrast_examples.en: I'll call you when I know (to a friend).

prompt.context_jp: Narrating that Kazuyuki had something he had to finish for his daughter by tonight

choices.text: 娘の理絵のために、今夜中にどうにか仕上げなければならない物があった。
物があった今夜中に、娘の理絵のために、どうにか仕上げなければならない。
仕上げなければならない娘の理絵のために物が今夜中にどうにかあった。

feedback.correct_en: A follows natural Japanese order: beneficiary → time → modifier-clause → head noun → existential verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: B and C shuffle elements in ways that break modifier-noun order and produce incoherent syntax.

contrast_examples.jp: 明日までにやらなければならないことがある。
contrast_examples.en: There's something I have to do by tomorrow.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供のために作る料理。
contrast_examples.en: A dish made for one's children.

prompt.context_jp: Mitsue announcing she'll take over as housewife
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Mitsue's dramatic declaration?

choices.text: 今日から私が この家の主婦になります
今日から私はこの家の主婦になります
今日から私を この家の主婦になります

feedback.correct_en: '私が' identifies Mitsue as THE one taking the role — an announcement/declaration with exhaustive-focus が. This is how the story actually renders her punchline.
feedback.incorrect_en: '私は' sounds like a neutral topic statement and loses the 'I, specifically, am claiming this role' impact. '私を' is ungrammatical here — 主婦になる takes the subject in が/は, not を.

contrast_examples.jp: 今日から私がリーダーになります。
contrast_examples.en: Starting today, I will be the leader (I'm the one).
